title: Lichfield Solar — digital ops & latency gotchas (scratch journal)
content:
Context: quick field notebook from call w/ Lichfield Solar (regional installer for rooftop + community microgrids). They want an assistant for ops teams: maintenance ticket summarization + voice-assisted checklists at edge with intermittent connectivity. This is personal scratchpad — messy, TODOs at bottom.

Meeting notes (2024-06-18)
- Attendees: Lichfield: Samir Patel (ops lead), Jody Mills (network), Tara Osei (field tech). Redwood: Anika (SE), Miguel (infra).
- High-level ask: run a small assistant locally at customer sites (private) to summarize events from field logs and provide verbal troubleshooting. Must work when internet is flaky; sync when back online.
- SLO target they care about: median response < 400ms for short answers (1-2 sentences) onsite; tail (95p) < 1.2s. For offline cached replies (local small-model) < 800ms.

Technical constraints / clarifications
- Hardware: 1x A10G-class edge appliance per site (low-power), sometimes older Intel SKUs for retrofits. Not all sites have GPUs — many are CPU-only.
- Network: satellite link on 30% of sites; NAT + CGNAT in provider network. Egress costs may be significant for frequent embeddings uploads.
- Data sensitivity: telemetry + occasional PII (technician notes w/ phone numbers). Must support KMS integration and log redaction.
- Model preferences: they want to try quantized open models (13B -> 4-bit) for local inference. Prefer fallback to hosted smaller model for heavy-lift analysis.
- Streaming: field techs want voice streaming and partial responses for checklists. Need support for WebSocket or long polling with incremental tokens.
- Caching: heavy reuse of prefix prompts (checklist templates). Prefix/KV cache likely high value.

Gotchas / risks called out on the call
- Cold start tail: small appliances sleep; wake-up + model load causes 10–30s cold starts. Need warm pool or snapshot loading.
- Batch vs interactive: batch batching saves cost but increases tail latency — unacceptable for voice-driven checks. Need per-connection low-latency path.
- Tokenized audio costs unknown: if we transcribe at edge and send embeddings, watch egress. Consider on-device VAD + batching transcripts.
- NAT traversal: secure tunnel from appliance to private control plane must support reconnection and session migration when IPs change. Current site ISP changes IPs weekly.
- Logging: customer asked for per-request traces correlated to site-id + job-id. Must not store raw PII in logs.

Quick implementation ideas (brainstorm)
- Hybrid: ship a tiny quantized assistant (Llama2-7B-QLoRA style or similar) for immediate Q/A and checklists. For heavy ops (root-cause analysis), route to hosted Redwood model with redaction + explicit consent sync window.
- Warm snapshots: pre-load model weights into swap-friendly memory map + use a lightweight health-check to keep model hot during business hours.
- Cache & prefix reuse: implement site-specific prefix cache for checklist templates; use deterministic hashing to reuse KV cache across similar prompts.
- Edge sync strategy: incremental delta sync for embeddings and logs; compress + encrypt; schedule large syncs during off-peak.
- Streaming: provide WebSocket streaming with per-token ACK and fall back to short-polling if tunnel drops.

Open questions to validate
- How many concurrent field techs per site? (Samir said 2–4 typical but could spike during incidents). Impacts local concurrency sizing.
- SLA on offline mode: how long should assistant function without cloud sync? (they implied up to 7 days).
- Backup model licensing: confirm compatibility with quantization approach (some license constraints).
- Observability retention: default 30 days? They asked for 90 days for audits. Cost impact.

Concrete next steps / owners
- Action: write a short feasibility note with 3 deployment patterns (edge-only, hybrid sync, cloud-only fallback) + rough cost proxy. Owner: Anika. Target: 2024-06-24. (linked to JIRA-ENG-1298)
- Action: infra runbook for NAT/tunnel reconnection and session migration. Owner: Miguel. Target: 2024-06-28.
- Action: prototype quantized 4-bit 13B on A10G-class VM and measure cold-start memory + load time. Owner: Priya. Target: 2024-07-02.
- Action: legal to check model licensing/redistribution. Owner: Samir (customer) + Redwood legal ping. Target: 2024-06-30.

Notes to self
- Bring up prefix cache design in next sync — show me micro-benchmarks: median cache hit latency, eviction policy.
- Demo idea: offline voice checklist + one-button sync; make video for execs.
- Watch concurrency interplay: 1-1 low-latency path for interactive voice, separate batch worker for embedding uploads.

Rough timeline sketch (for internal use)
- Week 1: feasibility doc + infra runbook + legal check.
- Week 2–3: prototype quantized model on representative hardware; measure cold start and inference latency for 1–4 concurrent sessions.
- Week 4: internal alpha at 2 pilot sites; collect telemetry and iterate.

Misc scribbles
- Consider local STT to reduce egress (Vosk or Kaldi-style on-device) — check accuracy for noisy rooftop environment.
- If egress limited, consider sending compressed embeddings every hour rather than raw transcripts.

END — will tidy and move to Confluence when draft stable.
